summary: Configured node1 to require new passwords of at least 12 characters and at least three character classes. The policy remained active and passed functional checks after reboot.
actions_performed: Installed Ubuntu's libpam-pwquality module and verification utility.
Enabled pam_pwquality in the common password PAM stack.
Verified rejection of passwords failing either boundary and acceptance of a compliant control.
Safely rebooted node1 and verified recovery and policy persistence.

evidence.requirement: New passwords must be at least 12 characters
evidence.summary: Configuration shows minlen=12; direct tests rejected an 11-character four-class candidate specifically for insufficient length, both before and after reboot.

evidence.requirement: New passwords must use at least three character classes
evidence.summary: Configuration shows minclass=3; direct tests rejected a 14-character two-class candidate specifically for insufficient classes and accepted a compliant control.

evidence.requirement: Password-quality policy is integrated into PAM
evidence.summary: libpam-pwquality is installed and pam_pwquality.so is active before pam_unix in /etc/pam.d/common-password.

Captured healthy baseline with boot ID a9593011-3617-4b72-8b02-2e8a4d2b17a3, received restart acknowledgement, observed new boot ID 577ce999-4ea9-4803-b604-df85efb9a326, and confirmed system/SSH health plus persistent functional policy enforcement.
